counterevidence_considered.description: The report also names a larger scheduled network of 96 stations, which was tested as possible evidence of a complete-domain target.

The report accounts for 24 scheduled stations outside the eligible set, but explicitly labels them outside the target set and not assessed rather than silently dropping them from a complete-domain claim.

source_refs.quoted_text: Planned-unit accounting: 18 eligible stations with an occurrence, 54 eligible stations without an occurrence, and 24 scheduled stations outside the eligible set and not assessed for occurrence.

evidence.description: The stated scientific question is explicitly conditional on passing the prespecified signal screen.

source_refs.quoted_text: Build a coastal-station workflow whose scientific question is the occurrence rate conditional on passing a prespecified signal screen.

evidence.description: The input semantics distinguish 72 signal-eligible assessed stations from 24 stations outside the eligible set and not assessed.
The report defines the target as the 72 signal-eligible stations and reports the selected rate only among those stations.

source_refs.quoted_text: Target population: 72 signal-eligible stations that passed the prespecified signal screen.
[selected-result] Among signal-eligible stations, the occurrence rate was 18/72 = 25%.

evidence.description: The workflow generates a conditional target and selected result using the same 72-station eligible domain.

TARGET_LINE = f'Target population: {SIGNAL_ELIGIBLE_STATIONS} signal-eligible stations that passed the prespecified signal screen.' + LF

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the conditional interpretation by checking whether the mention of a 96-station scheduled network was used as the target or in a complete-network selected claim. It was not: both the stated target and selected result are expressly limited to the 72 signal-eligible stations, while the other 24 are identified as outside that eligible set.
